Beyond the bump up to the M6 chip, the entry-level 14-inch MacBook features the same overall design and port layout as last year's M5 upgrade and, in fact, the year prior's M4 refresh. This means the new MacBook Pro features three Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, a MagSafe 3 charging port, a full HDMI port, and an SD card slot. While this isn't exactly surprising, given Apple's MacBook Pro design has been around for several years now, it would have been nice to see it evolve in some way. The colors are all the same too: Blue, Purple, Pink, Orange, Yellow, Green, and Silver. At the very least, it would have been great to see an iMac color refresh and a port selection that made a bit more sense. I love my MacBook Pro M5 and hope it lasts me as long as my M1 did. What confuses me is why so much emphasis is put on the device's bigger, better performance, but most people are running most things online now, so the performance is surely about the weakest link... Usually the speed of the internet and connection at the time you are using it. Nobody really focuses on that. I'm sure my Antigravity work sessions would be improved greatly by a much better and consistent internet connection than a slightly faster processor in my Mac. Just food for thought.

story.title: Apple refreshes the iMac, entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip

facts.text: Apple Inc. rolled out a new 24-inch iMac and an entry-level MacBook Pro with a 14-inch screen, marking a pair of key updates in an end-to-end overhaul of the company’s computer line.
The iMac is moving from an M4 processor, while the MacBook Pro received the M5 last year.
Apple has announced refreshes for the iMac and the entry-level, 14-inch MacBook Pro .
Both machines are getting the M6 chip, which was introduced in the Mac mini several weeks ago.
In this case, that means up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to double the Neural Engine performance.
Apple skipped the M5 and went straight to the M6 here.
It caps out at 32GB of RAM but can go to 4TB of storage.
Ahead of its upcoming "Pro and Tell" event, Apple has revealed its refreshed 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac , powered by its M6 chip.
This means the new MacBook Pro features three Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, a MagSafe 3 charging port, a full HDMI port, and an SD card slot.
While this isn't exactly surprising, given Apple's MacBook Pro design has been around for several years now, it would have been nice to see it evolve in some way.
Apple also refreshed its all-in-one iMac with the M6 chip .
This update comes two years after the colorful computer got the M4 chip (the iMac skipped the M5 series entirely).
The base M6 configuration in the iMac features a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, a step up from the 8-core M4 CPU in the last-generation iMac.

Apple says that the M6 features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, emphasizing that it's a powerful platform for local LLMs and that the chip is designed to take full advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.
The MacBook M6 also features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, alongside returning features like the 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and Liquid Retina XDR display with optional nano-texture.
The entry-level iMac starts at $1,500 and will be available to pre-order on October 28th, with shipping starting on November 6th.
Apple also recently revealed its A20-powered iPad mini .
At its upcoming event, the tech giant is expected to show off its long-rumored touchscreen MacBook for the first time.

extraction.body: The US power sector could release 42 percent more planet-heating carbon dioxide pollution by 2030 than it did in 2025 as it builds out more fossil fuel infrastructure to meet data center electricity demand, according to a new analysis by the Sierra Club. CO2 emissions from electricity generation would increase by 618 million tons by the end of the decade if planned AI projects are constructed. That’s roughly equivalent to carbon pollution from the electricity use of 128,788,523 homes in a year. The Sierra Club’s estimate is higher than some previous projections from other groups. Another study published by academic researchers in June forecast that electricity demand from data centers and crypto mines could push up power sector emissions by 28 percent by 2030 when compared to a scenario with no data center growth. The outcome depends on how many planned data center projects actually come to fruition, as well as on what type of technology is used to power those facilities. Net US greenhouse gas emission have fallen from a peak of about 6.58 billion metric tons in 2007 to about 5.35 billion metric tons in 2025. But that pollution started ticking back up last year as data centers drove up electricity demand. The Trump administration is incentivising the buildout of fossil fuel infrastructure for data centers while simultaneously rolling back pollution regulations and stalling renewable energy projects. The US is now planning to build more fossil fuel capacity than it has in a decade, according to a separate report published this month by the Environmental Defense Fund.

extraction.headline: Data centers could send US climate pollution skyrocketing
extraction.description: Gas plants built for data centers are poised to undo more than a decade of climate action.

relevantPassages.text: The US power sector could release 42 percent more planet-heating carbon dioxide pollution by 2030 than it did in 2025 as it builds out more fossil fuel infrastructure to meet data center electricity demand, according to a new analysis by the Sierra Club.
But that pollution started ticking back up last year as data centers drove up electricity demand.

sources.title: Home electricity bills are skyrocketing. For data centers, not so much. - Yale Climate Connections

extraction.body: Electricity prices in the U.S. are rising sharply, but the burden of rising bills isn’t evenly distributed. A Yale Climate Connections analysis of electricity prices has found that data centers and other commercial electricity users are consuming more kilowatts than ever, but the price they pay for that electricity has risen only a little. And industrial users of electricity are actually paying lower prices, on average, than they were two years ago. But between 2020 and 2024, residential electricity prices in the U.S. increased by 25%. In other words, people using their toasters, laptops, and electric heating and cooking at home are paying ever-increasing prices, while the data centers that are driving rapid growth in electricity demand are scoring handsome discounts. You'll receive the latest climate change news, tips, and inspiring stories twice a week. Sign up to be part of the solution today A word of warning: this analysis might make you mad, but hopefully in a productive way. Electricity customers are sorted into use types: residential for homes, commercial for businesses and data centers, and industrial for facilities like factories or refineries. The graph below shows how the prices paid by these three sectors have shifted over time. From 1997 through 2007, electricity prices for all three categories of users rose and fell at a similar pace. In 2008, that trend stopped. That year, electricity prices went up for residences but down for businesses and industries. Over the next decade, home uses of electricity became more expensive, while electricity prices for businesses stayed nearly flat. In 2021, the trend shifted again. Electricity prices for all three sectors began to rise steeply, but unequally. The gap between home energy use and business/industrial energy use became even larger. In the last two years, these differences became especially stark, as shown in the chart below. In just two years, starting in 2022, residential electricity prices rose by 10%, while commercial prices increased by only 3%, and industrial electricity prices fell by 2%. This is an example of the “ K-shaped economy ,” where things improve for some groups while getting worse for others. The lines on a K-shaped graph head off in different directions, illustrating an ever-larger gap between those benefiting and those left out. If any one sector is driving the growth in electricity usage, it would make sense for that sector to foot the bill for the power plants and power lines needed to serve their demand. So let’s look at how electricity use is growing in each sector. The chart below shows how the amount of electricity used by each sector has changed since 1997. Industrial use has stayed relatively flat, while commercial and residential use both grew at fairly similar rates and are now consuming about 40% more power than they were in 1997. But a new pattern emerged in the last three years, as seen in the chart below. Commercial demand for electricity rose sharply and steadily, using 9% more power over just a three-year span. Glenn McGrath, an electricity data analyst at the U.S. Energy Information Administration, wrote in an email that the growing energy needs of data centers “are likely a significant factor” behind increasing electricity use in the commercial sector. To sum up the situation in recent years, household electricity use has grown the least of the three sectors, but that’s where prices have gone up the most. The data illustrates how residential users are subsidizing the energy bills of A.I. and data centers, a perspective backed up by other recent analyses . A report by the Harvard Law School Environmental and Energy Law Program, Extracting Profits from the Public , lays out some of the reasons why Big Tech is able to off-load its costs onto the public and outlines specific steps policymakers can take to restore balance. We help millions of people better understand climate change and what to do about it. Help us reach even more people like you. But for individual consumers, the situation is the opposite. In many states, people have no choice in their energy provider or their energy prices, and they can’t look elsewhere for a better deal. In the parlance of the energy industry, everyday people are often called “captive ratepayers” because we have little choice but to be the ever-faithful customers of a monopoly utility. Rising electricity bills can trigger a host of negative consequences. High energy costs may prevent people from adequately heating or cooling their homes, which can contribute to both physical and mental health problems. Expensive energy can also lead people to forego necessities in other areas of their lives in order to keep up with rising bills and avoid having their service shut off. These burdens fall disproportionately on low-income, Black, Hispanic, and disadvantaged households, who spend a large portion of their income on energy bills. Higher electricity prices could also slow the adoption of modern, climate-friendly technology such as electric vehicles, heat pumps, and induction stoves that rely on electricity. That said, electric cars and appliances are more efficient than their fossil-fuel counterparts, so the trade-off is often still worth it. And in some cases, expensive electricity can spur faster adoption of climate solutions. Home solar panels pay for themselves more quickly, and energy conservation measures make even more financial sense than before. The electricity system in the U.S. is undergoing multiple stresses at once. Data centers seem to have an unquenchable thirst for energy, as extreme weather – often made worse by our warming climate – destabilizes the grid and causes spikes in electricity demand. At the same time, electricity generation is slowly transitioning from large, centralized power plants to numerous, distributed forms of electricity generation. But at the root of it all, the data suggests that everyday people are footing the bill while companies that consume ever more power are paying less. At a time when corporations seem to enjoy many structural advantages over consumers, from lower tax rates to relaxed pollution requirements , the burden of rising energy bills can make one feel powerless. And yes, the pun was intentional. Decisions about electricity rates are made by public utility commissions , which don’t usually get much attention – but that may be changing. In the November 2025 elections in Georgia, two incumbent public utility commissioners were resoundingly defeated after residential electricity prices climbed by 41% in just four years. Commissions are increasingly criticized for rubber-stamping price hikes and not protecting ratepayers who are caught inside a monopolistic system. If you’re interested in learning more about the electricity decision-making process near you, here’s a directory of public utility commissions in every state , and Canary Media wrote a user-friendly guide to engaging with your electricity regulators. The deck may feel stacked against the common person, but that might just be all the more reason to get involved. We love it when others republish our articles. passages: Electricity prices in the U.S. are rising sharply, but the burden of rising bills isn’t evenly distributed.

A Yale Climate Connections analysis of electricity prices has found that data centers and other commercial electricity users are consuming more kilowatts than ever, but the price they pay for that electricity has risen only a little. And industrial users of electricity are actually paying lower prices, on average, than they were two years ago.

But between 2020 and 2024, residential electricity prices in the U.S. increased by 25%. In other words, people using their toasters, laptops, and electric heating and cooking at home are paying ever-increasing prices, while the data centers that are driving rapid growth in electricity demand are scoring handsome discounts.
You'll receive the latest climate change news, tips, and inspiring stories twice a week. Sign up to be part of the solution today
A word of warning: this analysis might make you mad, but hopefully in a productive way.

Electricity customers are sorted into use types: residential for homes, commercial for businesses and data centers, and industrial for facilities like factories or refineries. The graph below shows how the prices paid by these three sectors have shifted over time.
From 1997 through 2007, electricity prices for all three categories of users rose and fell at a similar pace.
In 2008, that trend stopped. That year, electricity prices went up for residences but down for businesses and industries.
Over the next decade, home uses of electricity became more expensive, while electricity prices for businesses stayed nearly flat.

In 2021, the trend shifted again. Electricity prices for all three sectors began to rise steeply, but unequally. The gap between home energy use and business/industrial energy use became even larger. In the last two years, these differences became especially stark, as shown in the chart below.
In just two years, starting in 2022, residential electricity prices rose by 10%, while commercial prices increased by only 3%, and industrial electricity prices fell by 2%.

This is an example of the “ K-shaped economy ,” where things improve for some groups while getting worse for others. The lines on a K-shaped graph head off in different directions, illustrating an ever-larger gap between those benefiting and those left out.

If any one sector is driving the growth in electricity usage, it would make sense for that sector to foot the bill for the power plants and power lines needed to serve their demand. So let’s look at how electricity use is growing in each sector.

The chart below shows how the amount of electricity used by each sector has changed since 1997. Industrial use has stayed relatively flat, while commercial and residential use both grew at fairly similar rates and are now consuming about 40% more power than they were in 1997.
But a new pattern emerged in the last three years, as seen in the chart below. Commercial demand for electricity rose sharply and steadily, using 9% more power over just a three-year span.

Glenn McGrath, an electricity data analyst at the U.S. Energy Information Administration, wrote in an email that the growing energy needs of data centers “are likely a significant factor” behind increasing electricity use in the commercial sector.
To sum up the situation in recent years, household electricity use has grown the least of the three sectors, but that’s where prices have gone up the most.

The data illustrates how residential users are subsidizing the energy bills of A.I. and data centers, a perspective backed up by other recent analyses . A report by the Harvard Law School Environmental and Energy Law Program, Extracting Profits from the Public , lays out some of the reasons why Big Tech is able to off-load its costs onto the public and outlines specific steps policymakers can take to restore balance.
We help millions of people better understand climate change and what to do about it. Help us reach even more people like you.

But for individual consumers, the situation is the opposite. In many states, people have no choice in their energy provider or their energy prices, and they can’t look elsewhere for a better deal. In the parlance of the energy industry, everyday people are often called “captive ratepayers” because we have little choice but to be the ever-faithful customers of a monopoly utility.

Rising electricity bills can trigger a host of negative consequences. High energy costs may prevent people from adequately heating or cooling their homes, which can contribute to both physical and mental health problems. Expensive energy can also lead people to forego necessities in other areas of their lives in order to keep up with rising bills and avoid having their service shut off. These burdens fall disproportionately on low-income, Black, Hispanic, and disadvantaged households, who spend a large portion of their income on energy bills.

Higher electricity prices could also slow the adoption of modern, climate-friendly technology such as electric vehicles, heat pumps, and induction stoves that rely on electricity. That said, electric cars and appliances are more efficient than their fossil-fuel counterparts, so the trade-off is often still worth it.

And in some cases, expensive electricity can spur faster adoption of climate solutions. Home solar panels pay for themselves more quickly, and energy conservation measures make even more financial sense than before.

The electricity system in the U.S. is undergoing multiple stresses at once. Data centers seem to have an unquenchable thirst for energy, as extreme weather – often made worse by our warming climate – destabilizes the grid and causes spikes in electricity demand. At the same time, electricity generation is slowly transitioning from large, centralized power plants to numerous, distributed forms of electricity generation.

But at the root of it all, the data suggests that everyday people are footing the bill while companies that consume ever more power are paying less. At a time when corporations seem to enjoy many structural advantages over consumers, from lower tax rates to relaxed pollution requirements , the burden of rising energy bills can make one feel powerless. And yes, the pun was intentional.

Decisions about electricity rates are made by public utility commissions , which don’t usually get much attention – but that may be changing. In the November 2025 elections in Georgia, two incumbent public utility commissioners were resoundingly defeated after residential electricity prices climbed by 41% in just four years. Commissions are increasingly criticized for rubber-stamping price hikes and not protecting ratepayers who are caught inside a monopolistic system.

If you’re interested in learning more about the electricity decision-making process near you, here’s a directory of public utility commissions in every state , and Canary Media wrote a user-friendly guide to engaging with your electricity regulators. The deck may feel stacked against the common person, but that might just be all the more reason to get involved.

sources.title: Ameren Missouri Proposes Pollution-Heavy Future to Power Data Centers - CleanTechnica
passages: “The saying goes to stop digging if you’re in a hole, but Ameren is still digging with its pollution-heavy plan even though it admits extreme weather events are increasing.
Ameren and tech companies are gambling with the future of humanity as they power data centers with coal and gas.
SAINT LOUIS, Mo. — Late yesterday, Ameren Missouri filed a proposed long-range energy plan with its regulators at the Missouri Public Service Commission (PSC).

If approved as proposed, Ameren Missouri would significantly increase its reliance on fossil fuels, including a large increase in gas-burning power plants and extended coal-burning at its Labadie and Sioux plants.
Ironically, Ameren cites recent extreme weather as a justification for its gas-heavy investments, a plan that will exacerbate local climate disasters.
Extreme weather can also quickly send the price of gas skyrocketing, as was the case during Winter Storm Uri.

SAINT LOUIS, Mo. — Late yesterday, Ameren Missouri filed a proposed long-range energy plan with its regulators at the Missouri Public Service Commission (PSC). If approved as proposed, Ameren Missouri would significantly increase its reliance on fossil fuels, including a large increase in gas-burning power plants and extended coal-burning at its Labadie and Sioux plants. Labadie is the deadliest coal plant in the country. Ameren’s significant investment in new gas and continued coal burning coincides with the utility dropping its carbon dioxide emissions reduction goals from the promotional materials for its latest energy plan. Ironically, Ameren cites recent extreme weather as a justification for its gas-heavy investments, a plan that will exacerbate local climate disasters. Extreme weather can also quickly send the price of gas skyrocketing, as was the case during Winter Storm Uri. The Sierra Club actively intervenes when Ameren files its energy plans before the PSC. In previous years, Ameren admitted that it does not consider the public health impacts of the energy generation investments it makes, including new gas plants and coal plant extensions. Additionally, Ameren does not consider the climate impact of fugitive emissions from the extraction and transportation of natural gas, which is predominantly methane, a potent greenhouse gas. Ameren released its new energy plan against the backdrop of the Trump administration’s proposal to repeal the Endangerment Finding , the basis for regulating greenhouse gas emissions under the Clean Air Act. Significant and concerning changes to Ameren’s energy plan from last year include: Statement from Jenn DeRose, Sierra Club’s Beyond Coal Campaign Strategist in Missouri: “The saying goes to stop digging if you’re in a hole, but Ameren is still digging with its pollution-heavy plan even though it admits extreme weather events are increasing. Burning more coal and gas will only increase the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events like heatwaves, droughts, and floods. Ameren and tech companies are gambling with the future of humanity as they power data centers with coal and gas. We need Ameren to stop making bad investments for families and small businesses, and this plan is full of them. Unless elected officials, business owners and every customer start holding Ameren accountable, we’ll be stuck with an expensive and polluting electric grid that benefits billionaires and harms struggling families.” The Sierra Club is America’s largest and most influential grassroots environmental organization, with millions of members and supporters. passages: Utility Drops net-zero emissions reduction goal from promotional materials.

SAINT LOUIS, Mo. — Late yesterday, Ameren Missouri filed a proposed long-range energy plan with its regulators at the Missouri Public Service Commission (PSC). If approved as proposed, Ameren Missouri would significantly increase its reliance on fossil fuels, including a large increase in gas-burning power plants and extended coal-burning at its Labadie and Sioux plants. Labadie is the deadliest coal plant in the country.

Ameren’s significant investment in new gas and continued coal burning coincides with the utility dropping its carbon dioxide emissions reduction goals from the promotional materials for its latest energy plan. Ironically, Ameren cites recent extreme weather as a justification for its gas-heavy investments, a plan that will exacerbate local climate disasters. Extreme weather can also quickly send the price of gas skyrocketing, as was the case during Winter Storm Uri.

The Sierra Club actively intervenes when Ameren files its energy plans before the PSC. In previous years, Ameren admitted that it does not consider the public health impacts of the energy generation investments it makes, including new gas plants and coal plant extensions. Additionally, Ameren does not consider the climate impact of fugitive emissions from the extraction and transportation of natural gas, which is predominantly methane, a potent greenhouse gas.

Ameren released its new energy plan against the backdrop of the Trump administration’s proposal to repeal the Endangerment Finding , the basis for regulating greenhouse gas emissions under the Clean Air Act.
Significant and concerning changes to Ameren’s energy plan from last year include:
Statement from Jenn DeRose, Sierra Club’s Beyond Coal Campaign Strategist in Missouri:

“The saying goes to stop digging if you’re in a hole, but Ameren is still digging with its pollution-heavy plan even though it admits extreme weather events are increasing. Burning more coal and gas will only increase the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events like heatwaves, droughts, and floods. Ameren and tech companies are gambling with the future of humanity as they power data centers with coal and gas. We need Ameren to stop making bad investments for families and small businesses, and this plan is full of them. Unless elected officials, business owners and every customer start holding Ameren accountable, we’ll be stuck with an expensive and polluting electric grid that benefits billionaires and harms struggling families.”

The Sierra Club is America’s largest and most influential grassroots environmental organization, with millions of members and supporters. In addition to protecting every person's right to get outdoors and access the healing power of nature, the Sierra Club works to promote clean energy, safeguard the health of our communities, protect wildlife, and preserve our remaining wild places through grassroots activism, public education, lobbying, and legal action. The Sierra Club, one of the oldest environmental preservation organizations in the U.S., has now put forth an estimate that by 2030, U.S. data center buildouts will be outputting as much carbon dioxide as the entirety of Mexico, pushing back progress on greenhouse gas reduction by 15 years, Bloomberg reports.

An increasing number of countries and states are enacting laws demanding that new data center builds have a large portion of their power generated by green sources. However, those laws rarely apply retroactively, and oftentimes have a phase-in period. Even the Irish law on the matter demanding that new data centers be fed by 80% of renewable power only requires that that happens six years after they're powered up. In the current AI-driven market, speed of construction is king. Roughly 40% of U.S. data centers are fed by natural gas turbines , and the situation doesn't look like it'll be changing much. It'll likely get worse, as the addition of green sources almost assuredly won't keep up with demand. Much like RAM, GPUs, and storage, turbines were all slurped up by data centers. Their prices have risen by 50%, and production is backlogged for years, with one maker stating it's opening slots for production in 2032 . Having said all that, Brendan Pierpont from Energy Innovation, another climate-concerned organization, points out that although the current path looks dangerous for the environment, it's hard to make a hard prediction of how the situation will play out. He justifies his position with common data center roadblocks: the availability of turbines, delays in grid connections, and other delay factors. Truth be told, at this point it's hard to predict how many data centers will actually reach completion, given that requests for permits far exceed available grid capacity across the U.S., and a sizable number of buildouts are encountering strong opposition . extraction.body: The US power sector could release 42 percent more planet-heating carbon dioxide pollution by 2030 than it did in 2025 as it builds out more fossil fuel infrastructure to meet data center electricity demand, according to a new analysis by the Sierra Club. CO2 emissions from electricity generation would increase by 618 million tons by the end of the decade if planned AI projects are constructed. That’s roughly equivalent to carbon pollution from the electricity use of 128,788,523 homes in a year. The Sierra Club’s estimate is higher than some previous projections from other groups. Another study published by academic researchers in June forecast that electricity demand from data centers and crypto mines could push up power sector emissions by 28 percent by 2030 when compared to a scenario with no data center growth. The outcome depends on how many planned data center projects actually come to fruition, as well as on what type of technology is used to power those facilities. Net US greenhouse gas emission have fallen from a peak of about 6.58 billion metric tons in 2007 to about 5.35 billion metric tons in 2025. But that pollution started ticking back up last year as data centers drove up electricity demand. The Trump administration is incentivising the buildout of fossil fuel infrastructure for data centers while simultaneously rolling back pollution regulations and stalling renewable energy projects. The US is now planning to build more fossil fuel capacity than it has in a decade, according to a separate report published this month by the Environmental Defense Fund.

In other words, people using their toasters, laptops, and electric heating and cooking at home are paying ever-increasing prices, while the data centers that are driving rapid growth in electricity demand are scoring handsome discounts.

In 2021, the trend shifted again. Electricity prices for all three sectors began to rise steeply, but unequally. The gap between home energy use and business/industrial energy use became even larger. In the last two years, these differences became especially stark, as shown in the chart below.
In just two years, starting in 2022, residential electricity prices rose by 10%, while commercial prices increased by only 3%, and industrial electricity prices fell by 2%.

This is an example of the “ K-shaped economy ,” where things improve for some groups while getting worse for others. The lines on a K-shaped graph head off in different directions, illustrating an ever-larger gap between those benefiting and those left out.

If any one sector is driving the growth in electricity usage, it would make sense for that sector to foot the bill for the power plants and power lines needed to serve their demand. So let’s look at how electricity use is growing in each sector.

The chart below shows how the amount of electricity used by each sector has changed since 1997. Industrial use has stayed relatively flat, while commercial and residential use both grew at fairly similar rates and are now consuming about 40% more power than they were in 1997.
But a new pattern emerged in the last three years, as seen in the chart below. Commercial demand for electricity rose sharply and steadily, using 9% more power over just a three-year span.

Glenn McGrath, an electricity data analyst at the U.S. Energy Information Administration, wrote in an email that the growing energy needs of data centers “are likely a significant factor” behind increasing electricity use in the commercial sector.
To sum up the situation in recent years, household electricity use has grown the least of the three sectors, but that’s where prices have gone up the most.

The data illustrates how residential users are subsidizing the energy bills of A.I. and data centers, a perspective backed up by other recent analyses . A report by the Harvard Law School Environmental and Energy Law Program, Extracting Profits from the Public , lays out some of the reasons why Big Tech is able to off-load its costs onto the public and outlines specific steps policymakers can take to restore balance.

But for individual consumers, the situation is the opposite. In many states, people have no choice in their energy provider or their energy prices, and they can’t look elsewhere for a better deal. In the parlance of the energy industry, everyday people are often called “captive ratepayers” because we have little choice but to be the ever-faithful customers of a monopoly utility.

High energy costs may prevent people from adequately heating or cooling their homes, which can contribute to both physical and mental health problems. Expensive energy can also lead people to forego necessities in other areas of their lives in order to keep up with rising bills and avoid having their service shut off. Higher electricity prices could also slow the adoption of modern, climate-friendly technology such as electric vehicles, heat pumps, and induction stoves that rely on electricity. SAINT LOUIS, Mo. — Late yesterday, Ameren Missouri filed a proposed long-range energy plan with its regulators at the Missouri Public Service Commission (PSC).

SAINT LOUIS, Mo. — Late yesterday, Ameren Missouri filed a proposed long-range energy plan with its regulators at the Missouri Public Service Commission (PSC).

If approved as proposed, Ameren Missouri would significantly increase its reliance on fossil fuels, including a large increase in gas-burning power plants and extended coal-burning at its Labadie and Sioux plants.
Ironically, Ameren cites recent extreme weather as a justification for its gas-heavy investments, a plan that will exacerbate local climate disasters.
Extreme weather can also quickly send the price of gas skyrocketing, as was the case during Winter Storm Uri.

extraction.body: Apple on Tuesday unveiled its new 14-inch MacBook Pro, powered by its latest M6 chip. The new MacBook Pro has 24 hours of battery life and now supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity. The laptop starts at $1,999 and is available in space black and silver. Apple also announced its latest iMac , which is also powered by the M6 chip. The tech giant revealed the new devices just a day before its “Pro and Tell” event scheduled for Wednesday. On Monday, Apple announced its new iPad mini . The tech giant says the M6 chip features a 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core and a 12-core GPU that delivers more responsive performance, up to 30% faster graphics, and up to 25% faster AI workloads compared with the M5 chip. The M6 delivers up to 13 times the LLM prompt-processing speed of the M1 MacBook Pro and up to 1.3 times faster performance than the M5 model, Apple says. The M6 MacBook Pro starts with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, and has memory bandwidth of up to 170GB/s, up from the 153GB/s on the M5 chip. It includes HDMI, MagSafe 3, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, an SDXC card slot, and a headphone jack. Like previous models, the laptop features a 12-megapixel camera. The M6 MacBook Pro supports fast charging, reaching up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with a compatible high-wattage USB-C power adapter. As for the new M6-powered iMac, it features a faster CPU and GPU, with Neural Accelerators built into every core. Apple says the M6 delivers smooth multitasking and powerful performance for everyday apps, photo editing, and video production. The new iMac starts at $1,499 and comes in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver. The company also notes that the new iMac delivers up to five times faster on-device AI performance than the M4 model. It features a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, an advanced camera and audio system, up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports, color-matched accessories, and macOS 27. Both the new MacBook Pro and iMac can be preordered starting October 28 and will be available starting November 6. Aisha is a consumer news reporter at TechCrunch. Prior to joining the publication in 2021, she was a telecom reporter at MobileSyrup. extraction.body: Apple introduces :br(s):the new 14‑inch :br(s):MacBook Pro with M6 Supercharged by M6, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features incredible performance and next-level AI capabilities, enhanced connectivity, and up to 24 hours of battery life, delivering even more value CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 , delivering even more performance, powerful on-device AI capabilities, and faster connectivity for college students, business users, creators, and more. M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive. 1 The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5, making the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 a compelling value for users who need serious power. 2 For those upgrading from M1, the performance gains are even more significant, with up to 11x faster graphics and up to 13x faster AI performance. 3 With additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, M6 turns MacBook Pro into an even more powerful platform for AI — from taking advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features across apps and macOS to running LLMs locally, all while preserving user privacy. 4 In addition, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, while superfast storage makes working with large files, exporting projects, and running demanding AI workflows fly. And with phenomenal battery life of up to 24 hours, it delivers the same remarkable performance whether plugged in or on battery, so users can work, create, and pursue their passions from anywhere. 3 It also offers the advanced features users love, including the stunning Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, a 12MP Center Stage camera, an immersive six-speaker sound system, and a wide array of ports. Together with macOS 27, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is a major upgrade for existing Mac users and those coming to Mac for the first time. The company specifies 16GB of unified memory as standard, configurable to 32GB. Unified memory is a shared memory pool available to the chip’s processors. That capacity deserves attention alongside processing speed because software needs enough room to hold its working data.
For a buyer considering local AI, capacity and speed answer different questions. Capacity determines whether a workload fits comfortably. Speed determines how long supported work takes once it runs.

A faster processor cannot automatically make an oversized workload practical. Conversely, a smaller model that already fits can still benefit from reduced waiting. Those distinctions matter when reading a launch announcement organized around performance improvements.

The laptop also adds Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, the latest wireless generations listed for this model. Apple advertises up to 24 hours of battery life. Neither specification establishes how long a demanding local AI session will last.

T3’s coverage of the 14-inch hardware refresh highlights the combination of updated processing and connectivity. That combination gives the product a broader purpose than running AI demonstrations. A professional laptop still has to support ordinary work between demanding tasks.
The important change is therefore cumulative. Apple is adding resources to a machine expected to move between communication, development, creative applications, and occasional intensive processing.
A newer processor can help the first person only when the application benefits from it. The second person needs evidence about their working day, including the applications and settings they use.

This is where Apple’s own product history becomes useful. Its M5 GPU architecture already included a Neural Accelerator in each GPU core. Apple also described support through its software frameworks and development interfaces.

M6 therefore continues an established direction rather than introducing local AI capability to the Mac for the first time. Recent owners should ask what their existing applications cannot do satisfactorily.
Neither decision requires declaring the new machine unnecessary or essential for everyone. The announcement expands the available options, while the existing device determines the urgency.

That is also why comparisons against much older hardware need careful interpretation. They describe an upgrade path for that installed base. They do not establish the benefit for a person starting from a recent model.
Additional AI hardware creates an opportunity that software still has to use. The distinction becomes important when a chip-level claim turns into expectations about an entire application.

A local AI workload runs its model calculations on the device. A large language model, software trained to generate and interpret language, also needs supporting application logic around those calculations.

For example, answering a question about documents can involve finding files, extracting text, selecting relevant passages, generating an answer, and presenting evidence. Improving model processing addresses only part of that chain.
This is why application measurements deserve more attention than a single speed claim. A faster answer is useful when the application finds the correct material and preserves enough context.
If it selects the wrong document, greater processing speed simply delivers the wrong result sooner. That limitation belongs to the workflow rather than the chip.
Developers evaluating the M6 MacBook Pro should therefore separate different stages of an AI task. Loading a model, processing a prompt, and generating subsequent text are distinct operations.

A prompt is the input supplied to a model. A token is a unit of text the model processes or generates. Time to first token measures the delay before output begins, rather than the duration of the complete response.
The announcement verifies the product, while independent testing must establish its practical limits. Buyers should keep those two kinds of evidence separate.
Apple’s performance figures describe selected workloads and comparison systems. They should remain attributed to the company until appropriate independent measurements support broader conclusions.
Tom’s Guide’s M6 performance preview includes results from an M6 Mac mini as context. The publication explicitly cautions that performance will differ in the laptop.
That distinction matters. Results from another computer can suggest what to investigate, but they cannot replace measurements of the shipping MacBook Pro.
Buyers need to know how the laptop behaves during longer sessions. An operation that completes quickly can place different demands on a system than repeated work throughout an afternoon.
A buyer handling sensitive information should examine the application’s actual data flow. The presence of AI acceleration does not establish that every feature keeps every input on the device.

Apple’s announcement footnotes also distinguish hardware capability from software availability. Siri AI is described as a beta feature in macOS 27.2, with language and regional conditions. Some server-based features have daily limits.
Those details affect what a purchaser can use and under which conditions. They deserve attention even when the main interest is the laptop’s hardware.
A person replacing an unreliable machine can use the same framework on a shorter timetable. The goal is to understand which benefits are available now and which remain dependent on later software.

Apple has provided a clearer hardware direction with the M6 MacBook Pro. The useful next step is to connect that direction to a task you actually perform. Identify the delay, capacity limit, or reliability problem behind your interest in replacing a laptop. Then compare reviews and application tests against that specific need. Keep conventional work in the evaluation alongside AI features, especially when the computer must support a full working day. If your current machine already handles those tasks comfortably, wait for evidence of a meaningful improvement. If it does not, use the shipping product’s measured behavior to judge the replacement. coreStoryFacts.text: Apple on Tuesday unveiled its new 14-inch MacBook Pro, powered by its latest M6 chip.
The new MacBook Pro has 24 hours of battery life and now supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity.
The laptop starts at $1,999 and is available in space black and silver.
The M6 delivers up to 13 times the LLM prompt-processing speed of the M1 MacBook Pro and up to 1.3 times faster performance than the M5 model, Apple says.
The tech giant revealed the new devices just a day before its “Pro and Tell” event scheduled for Wednesday.
On Monday, Apple announced its new iPad mini .
Buy One Pass, Get a Second Free Cover more ground at TechCrunch’s ultimate founder bootcamp of the year by bringing your co-founder or partner for free Book before the BOGO deal expires
As for the new M6-powered iMac, it features a faster CPU and GPU, with Neural Accelerators built into every core.
Aisha is a consumer news reporter at TechCrunch.
Apple introduces :br(s):the new 14‑inch :br(s):MacBook Pro with M6
“With the powerful M6 chip, we’re taking performance to the next level, with a boost in CPU speed and graphics and even more powerful capabilities for on-device AI.

It is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, 6 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors.
It is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain.
As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 7 and designed to be recycled.
M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive.
And with phenomenal battery life of up to 24 hours, it delivers the same remarkable performance whether plugged in or on battery, so users can work, create, and pursue their passions from anywhere.

3 It also offers the advanced features users love, including the stunning Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, a 12MP Center Stage camera, an immersive six-speaker sound system, and a wide array of ports.
Available in space black and silver, it can be pre-ordered beginning tomorrow, October 28, with availability starting Friday, November 6.
The 12-core GPU, also with two additional cores, delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance when compared to M5.

Siri AI can draw on personal context to help users find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections.
Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence using a dedicated keyboard shortcut.
Users can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.
Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful.

In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user’s tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description.

extraction.body: Amazon has long had to deal with the reality that owners of its Echo smart speakers weren’t using its voice-controlled assistant, Alexa, to buy things, as it had hoped. The tech giant hasn’t given up on that dream yet: Its AI assistant, Alexa+, is getting new shopping-enabled features in the U.S. and Canada from today, including a shopping hub, tools to add items to recent orders, and personalized recommendations. The company has already been working on features that make Alexa+ more of a shopping assistant with abilities like automated deal tracking and automatic purchases. The former feature lets you set Alexa to alert you when items in your cart or list drop below a certain price point. If you also have automatic purchases set up, Alexa can immediately order an item when it reaches that target price. Now, Amazon says it’s turning its Echo devices with a screen — the Echo Show 15 and 21 — into a shopping hub with an interface that it’s calling the “Shopping Essentials” experience. From this dashboard, Amazon shoppers can track deliveries in real time, see information about recent orders, get reminders about household essentials they need to reorder, and view their shopping list and saved items. The screen would also let shoppers tap to see more products and add items directly to their cart and then check out. To access the new experience, Amazon users can say “Alexa, where’s my stuff?” or “Open Shopping Essentials.” Soon, a shopping widget will be available to add to the Echo device’s home screen, too. Alexa+ is also gaining the ability to recommend gifts. facts.text: Another new feature rolling out now will allow Alexa device owners to add items to an upcoming delivery at any time until the item leaves the warehouse.
This builds on a similar feature recently added to Amazon’s retail website and app, so it isn’t necessarily an Alexa+ exclusive, but the feature wasn’t live on Alexa devices so far.
Amazon says Alexa+ is now available to “tens of millions” of customers, and these new features are live for users in the U.S. and Canada.
While not everyone has been happy with Alexa+, the company says the percentage of users who downgraded back to the AI-free interface remains in the “very low single digits.”
Amazon has long had to deal with the reality that owners of its Echo smart speakers weren’t using its voice-controlled assistant, Alexa, to buy things, as it had hoped.
To access the new experience, Amazon users can say “Alexa, where’s my stuff?” or “Open Shopping Essentials.” Soon, a shopping widget will be available to add to the Echo device’s home screen, too.

From this dashboard, Amazon shoppers can track deliveries in real time, see information about recent orders, get reminders about household essentials they need to reorder, and view their shopping list and saved items.

The former feature lets you set Alexa to alert you when items in your cart or list drop below a certain price point.
If you also have automatic purchases set up, Alexa can immediately order an item when it reaches that target price.

You’ll be able to describe who you’re shopping for, or the occasion, and Alexa+ will display product suggestions on the screen, organized into categories.

extraction.body: French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion-parameter open source AI model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), allowing businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves. Nicknamed “Le Chonk,” the model was first introduced earlier this month . The release comes as competition between open-weight AI developers like Mistral and closed-model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic heats up, with the former arguing that businesses and governments shouldn’t have to rely on outside AI companies for access to advanced capabilities. That argument may hold more weight in cybersecurity, where organizations want more control over their data and systems. Or, as Mistral’s CEO, Arthur Mensch, explained, AI should “be a tool for empowerment, not dominance.” With Chonk, Mistral doubles down on that position, arguing that it’s able to achieve “state-of-the-art performance” at a “fraction of the compute and capital committed by closed labs.” The release of the model’s weights — the numerical training that animates the system — ensures that other companies and government agencies will now be able to deploy ML4 for their own purposes. Mistral says that its model is comparable in terms of performance with a Chinese open-weight competitor, GLM-5.3, which was previously considered one of the best open-weight models in the world — particularly when it comes to cyber work. However, Mistral’s model uses 47 percent fewer tokens per task, making it significantly more economical than GLM-5.3. The company also claims that the model outranks all other open models when it comes to agentic coding tasks on Artificial Analysis’ Coding Agent Index, an AI benchmarking site. “Amid growing cyber threats, ML4 brings state-of-the-art sovereign cyber defense capabilities to enterprises and governments globally,” the company said Thursday. “Enterprise and public sector institutions can now download, deploy, and own frontier AI to detect, analyze, and respond to threats across code and IT infrastructure.” The weights for ML4 are being made available on Hugging Face and via its API. Pierre Stock, Vice President of Science at Mistral, told TechCrunch that the release of the model’s weights meant that organizations will have more control over how they use AI to defend themselves. “Concretely, it means that, for instance, as a business company or as a government, you’re able to have access to frontier intelligence to defend yourselves against cyberattacks. Access that can’t be cut off by definition because the model is open-weighted,” he said. Stock added that the model could be used to “identify, coordinate, and respond in real time to major security incidents, and that the open sourcing means that companies can deploy this model on-prem in their own ecosystem. While advances in AI cybersecurity are helping security professionals to find bugs at a much higher rate than before, Stock continued, he believes it’s important for companies to “provide [this same] capability to everyone…as soon as possible to ramp up and to strengthen the ecosystem,” given that “some malicious actors might try to actually leverage their own technology to attack.” Separately, Stock addressed concerns about recent incidents involving rogue AI agents, acknowledging the risks but cautioning against overreacting. “We don’t want to fearmonger people. We think it’s a problem that is solvable. It’s a hard problem to have good security,” he said. passages: French AI lab Mistral AI has released Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a new large multimodal model intended to compete with both American and Chinese rivals, in line with what French President Emmanuel Macron has described as a third way in AI.
Nicknamed Le Chonk in reference to its 1 trillion parameters, ML4 is positioned as an alternative to closed models that can be unplugged and to open models that are often made in China.
For now, it is accessible only through a public guardrail endpoint, with Mistral planning to release the weights in three weeks once safety testing is complete.
AI Insider is a Resonance portfolio company delivering AI-focused news, market intelligence, advisory and due diligence services to investors, enterprises and government agencies worldwide.
Stock said ML4 was trained entirely on Mistral’s own compute using 4,000 Nvidia GPUs, two to three times fewer than Chinese competitors and significantly fewer than closed-source rivals.
With benchmark results pending, Mistral hopes the model will lead its open-weight class and outperform closed models in targeted areas.

According to Stock, optimized use cases include cybersecurity, finance and chip design, the latter core to backers ASML, which led Mistral’s Series C, and Samsung, which led its Series D last month at a €21 billion valuation.

extraction.body: French artificial intelligence company Mistral AI officially launched the public preview of its next-generation flagship model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), codenamed "Le Chonk," on October 6 local time. This is the largest open-weight model by parameter count ever released in Europe, with 1 trillion total parameters and 49 billion active parameters. Starting today, developers can access the preview API through Mistral Studio, with model weights scheduled for open download at the end of this month. The Paris-based AI lab stated that ML4 is a natively multimodal model employing a sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture, activating only 49 billion parameters at any given moment, with each token dynamically routed to specialized sub-networks. This design compresses actual computational costs significantly while maintaining trillion-parameter-level inference depth. The model can process text and image inputs simultaneously, with attention layers optimized to natively support over 160 languages, covering all official EU languages. On the training infrastructure front, ML4 was trained entirely within Mistral's self-built data centers in Europe. The company disclosed the use of approximately 4,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs, with training conducted from scratch over two months, incorporating reinforcement learning pipelines to enhance reasoning, coding, agentic workflows, and human alignment capabilities. Mistral emphasized that its European deployment is operated end-to-end independently by the company, strictly adhering to EU laws and regulations, without being subject to any third-party digital service provider constraints. Notably, Tencent News cited an IT Home report stating that training used 3,800 GPUs, while Wccftech reported 4,000 GPUs. There is a slight discrepancy between the two figures, and Mistral has not yet provided a unified official statement. Mistral is collaborating with top-tier cybersecurity firms, trusted partners, and government regulators to conduct red-team testing of ML4 in real-world business environments. Partner organizations have been granted dedicated testing access. Unlike highly aligned closed-source models, ML4 employs an adaptable structured safety policy, capable of proactively analyzing malware, reproducing vulnerabilities, and deploying patches. The test version has moderately relaxed content safety review policies while strengthening offensive and defensive cybersecurity capabilities. This design orientation aligns with Mistral's consistent "open but responsible" philosophy. Company founder Arthur Mensch has repeatedly stated publicly that Europe needs its own frontier models and cannot rely entirely on technology supply from the United States or China. ML4's release is seen as a landmark move in Europe's sovereign AI infrastructure race. In comprehensive benchmarks, ML4 is described by Mistral as "the best open-weight model from the United States or Europe," achieving the highest levels among open-source models on critical enterprise workloads including cybersecurity, finance, legal, and manufacturing. In specific areas such as visual grounding, its performance even surpasses some frontier closed-source models. Data from independent evaluation firm Artificial Analysis shows ML4 scoring 38 on the firm's Intelligence Index, described as "the smartest model outside the US and China." On the Cybersecurity Index, ML4 scored 50, tying with Zhipu's GLM-5.3-Flash but trailing Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Pro at 56. On the DeepSWE v1.1 benchmark measuring long-horizon software engineering capabilities, ML4 scored 62%, surpassing GLM-5.3. However, Wccftech noted that when selecting the best published configurations for each model, GLM-5.3 and Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 both score around 69% on the DeepSWE live leaderboard, while GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Claude Opus 5 are around 74%, indicating a significant gap remains between ML4 and frontier closed-source models. One striking detail is that the only benchmark where ML4 genuinely leads is Harvey's Legal Agent, which measures model performance on real-world legal tasks including regulatory comprehension and compliance handling. Wccftech commented that this European model's only substantive lead is on "regulatory" benchmarks—a fitting characteristic for a European large language model. ML4's API pricing is set at $1.36 per million input tokens (~9.1 yuan), $4.18 per million output tokens (~28.1 yuan), and $0.14 per million cached input tokens. According to Artificial Analysis calculations, the standard cost per Intelligence Index task is approximately $1.13. Note: The context window of 524,288 tokens is below the 1 million token standard currently supported by most Chinese open-weight models. ML4's release pushes European open-weight model competition to a new level. Prior to this, Europe lacked products in this arena capable of competing head-to-head with Meta's Llama series from the US, Alibaba's Qwen series from China, and DeepSeek. Mistral's entry at trillion-parameter scale, coupled with the European sovereignty narrative and compliance advantages, targets enterprise customers with strict requirements for data residency and regulatory compliance—particularly EU public sector institutions, financial institutions, and defense-related industries. However, the challenges facing ML4 are equally significant. Its context window of only 524,288 tokens is roughly half that of mainstream Chinese open-weight models. On practical engineering capability benchmarks like DeepSWE, the gap with closed-source frontier models persists. On pricing, $1.36 per million input tokens places it in the mid-to-high range among open-weight models, making it less than optimal for price-sensitive small and medium developers. From a broader perspective, ML4's release reinforces the tripolar structure of global AI competition: the United States leads with closed-source frontier models, China continues to push forward on open-weight models, and Europe is attempting to carve out differentiation through "sovereignty + compliance." Whether Mistral can establish a foothold in the European domestic market with ML4 and achieve sufficient adoption within the global developer community will depend on the actual ecosystem feedback following the release of weights at month-end. On the DeepSWE v1.1 benchmark measuring long-horizon software engineering capabilities, ML4 scored 62%, surpassing GLM-5.3. However, Wccftech noted that when selecting the best published configurations for each model, GLM-5.3 and Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 both score around 69% on the DeepSWE live leaderboard, while GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Claude Opus 5 are around 74%, indicating a significant gap remains between ML4 and frontier closed-source models.

One striking detail is that the only benchmark where ML4 genuinely leads is Harvey's Legal Agent, which measures model performance on real-world legal tasks including regulatory comprehension and compliance handling. Wccftech commented that this European model's only substantive lead is on "regulatory" benchmarks—a fitting characteristic for a European large language model.

ML4's API pricing is set at $1.36 per million input tokens (~9.1 yuan), $4.18 per million output tokens (~28.1 yuan), and $0.14 per million cached input tokens. According to Artificial Analysis calculations, the standard cost per Intelligence Index task is approximately $1.13.
Note: The context window of 524,288 tokens is below the 1 million token standard currently supported by most Chinese open-weight models.

ML4's release pushes European open-weight model competition to a new level. Prior to this, Europe lacked products in this arena capable of competing head-to-head with Meta's Llama series from the US, Alibaba's Qwen series from China, and DeepSeek. Mistral's entry at trillion-parameter scale, coupled with the European sovereignty narrative and compliance advantages, targets enterprise customers with strict requirements for data residency and regulatory compliance—particularly EU public sector institutions, financial institutions, and defense-related industries.

However, the challenges facing ML4 are equally significant. Its context window of only 524,288 tokens is roughly half that of mainstream Chinese open-weight models. On practical engineering capability benchmarks like DeepSWE, the gap with closed-source frontier models persists. On pricing, $1.36 per million input tokens places it in the mid-to-high range among open-weight models, making it less than optimal for price-sensitive small and medium developers.

From a broader perspective, ML4's release reinforces the tripolar structure of global AI competition: the United States leads with closed-source frontier models, China continues to push forward on open-weight models, and Europe is attempting to carve out differentiation through "sovereignty + compliance." Whether Mistral can establish a foothold in the European domestic market with ML4 and achieve sufficient adoption within the global developer community will depend on the actual ecosystem feedback following the release of weights at month-end.

coreStoryFacts.text: French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion-parameter open source AI model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), allowing businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves.
Nicknamed “Le Chonk,” the model was first introduced earlier this month .
That argument may hold more weight in cybersecurity, where organizations want more control over their data and systems.

Or, as Mistral’s CEO, Arthur Mensch, explained, AI should “be a tool for empowerment, not dominance.” With Chonk, Mistral doubles down on that position, arguing that it’s able to achieve “state-of-the-art performance” at a “fraction of the compute and capital committed by closed labs.”

French AI lab Mistral AI has released Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a new large multimodal model intended to compete with both American and Chinese rivals, in line with what French President Emmanuel Macron has described as a third way in AI.
Nicknamed Le Chonk in reference to its 1 trillion parameters, ML4 is positioned as an alternative to closed models that can be unplugged and to open models that are often made in China.
For now, it is accessible only through a public guardrail endpoint, with Mistral planning to release the weights in three weeks once safety testing is complete.
AI Insider is a Resonance portfolio company delivering AI-focused news, market intelligence, advisory and due diligence services to investors, enterprises and government agencies worldwide.
Stock said ML4 was trained entirely on Mistral’s own compute using 4,000 Nvidia GPUs, two to three times fewer than Chinese competitors and significantly fewer than closed-source rivals.
With benchmark results pending, Mistral hopes the model will lead its open-weight class and outperform closed models in targeted areas.

According to Stock, optimized use cases include cybersecurity, finance and chip design, the latter core to backers ASML, which led Mistral’s Series C, and Samsung, which led its Series D last month at a €21 billion valuation.

He added that open-weight models are easier to audit, a growing priority for Mistral’s enterprise and institutional customers.

Independent benchmarking firm Artificial Analysis places Le Chonk below OpenAI and Anthropic flagship models.
Among non-Chinese LLMs users can download, Mistral performs well.
Multimodal and reasoning-capable, it uses a mixture of experts architecture with about 49 billion active parameters.
That design keeps serving costs lower than a dense model of the same total size.
Mistral did not publish hardware requirements in its release blog.
The company said the model remains small enough to run on 8-way GPU boxes such as Nvidia's HGX B300 or AMD's MI355X.
Mistral built Le Chonk inside European borders to meet demand for frontier-class models trained and run in the region.

extraction.body: French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion-parameter open source AI model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), allowing businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves. Nicknamed “Le Chonk,” the model was first introduced earlier this month . The release comes as competition between open-weight AI developers like Mistral and closed-model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic heats up, with the former arguing that businesses and governments shouldn’t have to rely on outside AI companies for access to advanced capabilities. That argument may hold more weight in cybersecurity, where organizations want more control over their data and systems. Or, as Mistral’s CEO, Arthur Mensch, explained, AI should “be a tool for empowerment, not dominance.” With Chonk, Mistral doubles down on that position, arguing that it’s able to achieve “state-of-the-art performance” at a “fraction of the compute and capital committed by closed labs.” The release of the model’s weights — the numerical training that animates the system — ensures that other companies and government agencies will now be able to deploy ML4 for their own purposes. Mistral says that its model is comparable in terms of performance with a Chinese open-weight competitor, GLM-5.3, which was previously considered one of the best open-weight models in the world — particularly when it comes to cyber work. However, Mistral’s model uses 47 percent fewer tokens per task, making it significantly more economical than GLM-5.3. The company also claims that the model outranks all other open models when it comes to agentic coding tasks on Artificial Analysis’ Coding Agent Index, an AI benchmarking site. “Amid growing cyber threats, ML4 brings state-of-the-art sovereign cyber defense capabilities to enterprises and governments globally,” the company said Thursday. “Enterprise and public sector institutions can now download, deploy, and own frontier AI to detect, analyze, and respond to threats across code and IT infrastructure.” The weights for ML4 are being made available on Hugging Face and via its API. passages: French AI lab Mistral AI has released Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a new large multimodal model intended to compete with both American and Chinese rivals, in line with what French President Emmanuel Macron has described as a third way in AI.
Nicknamed Le Chonk in reference to its 1 trillion parameters, ML4 is positioned as an alternative to closed models that can be unplugged and to open models that are often made in China.
For now, it is accessible only through a public guardrail endpoint, with Mistral planning to release the weights in three weeks once safety testing is complete.
AI Insider is a Resonance portfolio company delivering AI-focused news, market intelligence, advisory and due diligence services to investors, enterprises and government agencies worldwide.
Stock said ML4 was trained entirely on Mistral’s own compute using 4,000 Nvidia GPUs, two to three times fewer than Chinese competitors and significantly fewer than closed-source rivals.
With benchmark results pending, Mistral hopes the model will lead its open-weight class and outperform closed models in targeted areas.

According to Stock, optimized use cases include cybersecurity, finance and chip design, the latter core to backers ASML, which led Mistral’s Series C, and Samsung, which led its Series D last month at a €21 billion valuation.

Mistral VP Science Pierre Stock told TechCrunch that the company will work with trusted partners and governments in the meantime to ensure the open weights can be used for defense rather than malicious attacks.
He added that open-weight models are easier to audit, a growing priority for Mistral’s enterprise and institutional customers.

extraction.body: French artificial intelligence company Mistral AI officially launched the public preview of its next-generation flagship model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), codenamed "Le Chonk," on October 6 local time. This is the largest open-weight model by parameter count ever released in Europe, with 1 trillion total parameters and 49 billion active parameters. Starting today, developers can access the preview API through Mistral Studio, with model weights scheduled for open download at the end of this month. The Paris-based AI lab stated that ML4 is a natively multimodal model employing a sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture, activating only 49 billion parameters at any given moment, with each token dynamically routed to specialized sub-networks. This design compresses actual computational costs significantly while maintaining trillion-parameter-level inference depth. The model can process text and image inputs simultaneously, with attention layers optimized to natively support over 160 languages, covering all official EU languages. On the training infrastructure front, ML4 was trained entirely within Mistral's self-built data centers in Europe. The company disclosed the use of approximately 4,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs, with training conducted from scratch over two months, incorporating reinforcement learning pipelines to enhance reasoning, coding, agentic workflows, and human alignment capabilities. facts.text: French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion-parameter open source AI model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), allowing businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves.
Nicknamed “Le Chonk,” the model was first introduced earlier this month .
That argument may hold more weight in cybersecurity, where organizations want more control over their data and systems.

Mistral says that its model is comparable in terms of performance with a Chinese open-weight competitor, GLM-5.3, which was previously considered one of the best open-weight models in the world — particularly when it comes to cyber work.

Or, as Mistral’s CEO, Arthur Mensch, explained, AI should “be a tool for empowerment, not dominance.” With Chonk, Mistral doubles down on that position, arguing that it’s able to achieve “state-of-the-art performance” at a “fraction of the compute and capital committed by closed labs.”

French AI lab Mistral AI has released Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a new large multimodal model intended to compete with both American and Chinese rivals, in line with what French President Emmanuel Macron has described as a third way in AI.
Nicknamed Le Chonk in reference to its 1 trillion parameters, ML4 is positioned as an alternative to closed models that can be unplugged and to open models that are often made in China.
For now, it is accessible only through a public guardrail endpoint, with Mistral planning to release the weights in three weeks once safety testing is complete.
AI Insider is a Resonance portfolio company delivering AI-focused news, market intelligence, advisory and due diligence services to investors, enterprises and government agencies worldwide.
Stock said ML4 was trained entirely on Mistral’s own compute using 4,000 Nvidia GPUs, two to three times fewer than Chinese competitors and significantly fewer than closed-source rivals.
With benchmark results pending, Mistral hopes the model will lead its open-weight class and outperform closed models in targeted areas.

According to Stock, optimized use cases include cybersecurity, finance and chip design, the latter core to backers ASML, which led Mistral’s Series C, and Samsung, which led its Series D last month at a €21 billion valuation.

Mistral VP Science Pierre Stock told TechCrunch that the company will work with trusted partners and governments in the meantime to ensure the open weights can be used for defense rather than malicious attacks.
He added that open-weight models are easier to audit, a growing priority for Mistral’s enterprise and institutional customers.
Mistral released Mistral Large 4, a one trillion-parameter open weights model the company nicknamed Le Chonk, trained in European datacenters on 3,800 Grace Blackwell GPUs.
Weights go live on Hugging Face later this month.
Mistral's newest large language model carries one trillion parameters and a cat-meme nickname.
Independent benchmarking firm Artificial Analysis places Le Chonk below OpenAI and Anthropic flagship models.
Among non-Chinese LLMs users can download, Mistral performs well.

That design keeps serving costs lower than a dense model of the same total size.
Mistral did not publish hardware requirements in its release blog.
The company said the model remains small enough to run on 8-way GPU boxes such as Nvidia's HGX B300 or AMD's MI355X.
Mistral built Le Chonk inside European borders to meet demand for frontier-class models trained and run in the region.
Le Chonk opens a series of new models Mistral plans to release.
The company closed a €3 billion, about $3.4 billion, Series D funding round last month.
Mistral expects performance to improve as it continues applying reinforcement learning.
"Provider-level refusals can block legitimate vulnerability research and incident response, and where losing access to a capability mid-incident can itself become a critical security risk.

The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, 1 Live Activities, and Siri AI.
2 And with up to 24 hours of battery life in thinner and much lighter 3- and 4-pound designs, MacBook Pro is more portable than ever, empowering pros to take their work wherever inspiration strikes.

“PROLED XDR is the world’s best laptop display.
It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.

2020 coverage for HDR video editing and color grading.

Both color spaces are accessible within a single default preset, streamlining pro workflows and making it seamless to switch between them.
7 And macOS makes the most of the graphics, memory, and machine learning capabilities of Apple silicon, so apps perform at incredible speed.

Pros can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.
Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users.

And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love.

In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 provide fast, reliable wireless connectivity, and Touch ID enables a quick, easy, and secure login experience.
3 In addition, storage is now configurable up to 16TB.
Updated system gesture APIs also enable developers to create intuitive experiences designed specifically for Touch.
